observations: Photo 0 shows a brown Nikon D750 box with packing tape and torn corners, next to a smaller Nikkor Lens 50 box and a white Zhiyun box in the background.
Photo 1 shows the D750 box opened, containing Nikon manuals including a D750 User's Manual.
Photo 2 shows two bubble-wrapped items inside the box; the camera body itself is not visible.
A watermark reading POSTED ON OLAJIDE AMOS BISHOP appears across the photos.

claims.evidence: photo 0 box and photo 1 manual read D750; separate lens box suggests body-only sale
no origin documents or receipts visible in any photo
photo 0 shows the box taped and torn, not as-new packaging
camera is not shown powered on or tested in any photo

risks.risk: The box may be empty or contain a non-camera item; the actual body is never shown, only bubble wrap.
risks.proof: clear photo of the actual Nikon D750 body outside the box, showing serial number, lens mount, and condition.
risks.if_unproven: priced as empty box or non-working camera

risks.risk: The camera may not function (shutter, sensor, electronics) despite the claim.
risks.proof: video of the camera powering on, taking a photo, and displaying the image on the screen.

risks.risk: Shutter count and wear may be high despite the as-new claim.
risks.proof: photo of the menu showing shutter count or EXIF data from a recent photo.

risks.risk: American used origin cannot be verified; it may be locally used or refurbished.
risks.proof: purchase receipt or customs documentation showing US origin.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown origin or locally used

proof_requests: Photo of the actual Nikon D750 body outside the box with serial number visible.
Video of the camera powering on, taking a shot, and reviewing the image.
Screenshot or photo of the shutter count / camera menu.
response.reason: The Nikon D750 identity is readable on the box and manual, but the camera itself is unseen and untested, so it must be priced at worst case as non-working or missing.
